title: Design Hestia, the continuity role, with Hades cleanup folded in
summary: Write docs/design/hestia.md for Sri and the brain: one design for a continuity role (sanity checks and tidiness, per the BRIEF.md 2026-10-25 addendum), grounded in the eight named failures. Each gets a check, a code-or-model call, a cadence and fix-or-report. Add a proposed decision to docs/decisions.md and a CHANGELOG line. No code.

defaults_applied.how: Design written for an outside reader, defining Hestia, Hades and the eight failures in plain terms.
Claims cite BRIEF.md, D127 and the repository; unmeasured numbers are labeled estimates.
Alternatives are written down and the decision stays proposed, for review before any build.
One design file, one proposed decision, one changelog line; the build is split into one-producer jobs.
Criteria check each item's check, cadence and fix-or-report, not just the file's existence.
The design says which checks are enforced by code and marks prose-only rules.
Design requires that an empty findings list is reported with the checks that ran, never counted as success alone.
No secrets, personal data or email addresses in the docs.
Findings are measured by resolved problems and time to resolution, not by sweeps run.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: a reviewable design Sri and the brain can accept or amend before any Hestia code is built; audience is Sri, the brain and the later producers of the build jobs.
The next decision number is D129 (D128 is the last heading found); the producer should confirm by reading the end of docs/decisions.md.
Hestia reports and makes small fixes only; it does not gate work, per D127. Governance files are not changed.

Facts about the eight failures (disk fill, stale binary, never-pushed checkpoints, budgets) come from the request and are cited as stated unless the producer can confirm them in the repository; records/ is not available to check them.

Fixes Hestia does itself are small jobs through the normal change pipeline, not direct edits; destructive cleanup (deleting branches, worktrees, caches) is limited to what is provably Athena's own and merged, otherwise reported.
docs/decision-links.toml may need an entry if a test requires every decision to be linked; otherwise unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/hestia.md has a section or table row for each of the eight items: queued requests done or superseded; leftover branches, worktrees and build caches (citing the 2026-10-23 disk-full cache); checkpoints never pushed; installed binary older than its source; prompt budgets nearly full; the unevaluated keep rule; athena propose never run; docs that no longer match the code. Each row states the check, whether it is deterministic code or needs a model, its cadence, and whether Hestia fixes it as a small job or reports a work item.

The design states Hestia's budget (dollars and wall time per run, in total, with a stop rule) and how findings are measured (for example findings per run, true-positive rate on spot check, time from appearance to resolution). It labels every number as an estimate or says where it was measured. It also says how Hades's cleanup is folded in and when it would split out.

The design lists alternatives (for example: model-only sweeps, separate Hades now, folding into the scope guard of D127) and states the boundary with Artemis (D127 says Hestia does not gate work), with sources cited from BRIEF.md and the repository.

docs/decisions.md gains one new entry, numbered after D128, with status proposed (not accepted), in the same fields as neighbouring entries (Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost, Provenance), inserted as a top-level entry and not inside another.
The design has a build plan of numbered jobs, each sized for one producer run, with deliverables, a test or behavior check, and dependencies, with the deterministic checks first.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the design and the proposed decision, matching the file's existing format. No code, athena.toml or defaults.toml file changes.
Run `cargo test` and `cargo fmt --check` from the repository root; both pass, which shows that existing doc-linking or decision-numbering tests accept the new entry and design file.

out_of_scope: Any Rust code, CLI commands or crates for Hestia
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflows
Accepting the decision or queueing the build jobs
Actually cleaning branches, caches or the queue
Changing the Artemis scope guard design
departures: Slightly higher cost and lower pass chance than reference: a long multi-part design with many required elements, and decisions.md is a very large file where a misplaced insertion has been rejected before (D128).
